variants.headline: The treasury slips into deficit
body: The books have turned: the treasury now pays out {{deficit}} gold more than it collects each season. A sailmaker who fills orders for the {{terms.civic.government}} has begun asking for half his money up front. At the harbor, his apprentices were told to finish the sails already cut and to wait for the rest.

variants.headline: The books, newly behind
body: Last reckoning: receipts covered spending.
This reckoning: spending runs ahead.
The gap: {{deficit}} gold each turn, with no end named.

variants.headline: A bill that comes back every season
body: A shortfall of {{deficit}} gold each turn has opened in the accounts, the kind of gap that arrives quietly and stays. One warehouse sold or one road postponed would cover this season, but the same gap waits on the other side of the sale. A minister who will not name the expense to be cut is asking the public to fund a habit. The next count will show whether the shortfall came from a bad season or a new way of spending.

variants.headline: Sir, the treasury now outspends its income
body: Sir, I sell fish at the north market, and I know a bad week before the bells ring. The treasury is {{deficit}} gold behind every season, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has not said whose purse will make it good. When my own ledger runs red I sell a net or eat less. Which of those has the treasury chosen?

variants.headline: The treasury passes a thousand gold
body: Word from the counting room is that the reserve now stands at {{gold}} gold, {{gain}} more than at the last count and past a thousand. At the pay window, a mason with a bill for the new drain asked whether the chest was as full as the street said. The clerk counted the sum out twice before he answered.

variants.headline: The reserve reaches the thousand mark
body: We are informed that the public chest now contains {{gold}} gold, having gained {{gain}} since the last accounting, and that the sum has carried the reserve past a thousand. Among the older houses of the capital, we hear, the talk turns on the vault's new weight and on whether it will steady the notes and promises that circulate in its name.

variants.headline: Hear it! A thousand gold in the vault!
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}, hear it! The vault stands past a thousand, and the count today is {{gold}} gold! A thousand and more, counted in the open and counted twice! Bring your plans to the square, for there is coin to build with.

variants.headline: The treasury just crossed 1,000 gold
body: Treasury reserve just crossed a thousand. Exact figure: {{gold}} gold, up {{gain}}. No estimate, no rounding. The vault has the coin.

variants.headline: The treasury gains time against the deficit
body: Cover at the treasury has lengthened to {{turnsLeft}}, with {{gold}} gold in hand against {{deficit}} going out each season. That is more room than the last count allowed, and the clerk at the pay window has stopped turning away the smaller claims. He still writes every name in the book.

variants.headline: What the treasury can do with more time
body: The shortfall has not gone anywhere: {{deficit}} gold still leaves the treasury every season. But the reserve now covers {{turnsLeft}}, and that buys the {{terms.civic.government}} something no tax can: time. At the customs shed by the river, a clerk has been given a list of overdue accounts and a fortnight to walk it. If the money comes in, the season may close without a new levy. The gain lasts only while spending stays near today's figure.

variants.headline: The count runs long at the money-changer's table
body: On Tuesday the money-changers at the bridge had good news for once. They counted {{gold}} gold in the chest against {{deficit}} going out each season, and the total came to {{turnsLeft}} of cover. One of them laughed and put his scales away. The other kept his coat on.

variants.headline: The treasury reserve runs short
body: The chest holds {{turnsLeft}} of cover, with {{gold}} gold against {{deficit}} each turn. Down at the ropewalk, the owner has begun delivering twine in smaller lots and asking to be paid on the day. His men say the work has never come in so slow. Nobody at the yard expects the arrangement to last the season.

variants.headline: The treasury, counted
body: In the chest: {{gold}} gold.
Spending beyond receipts each season: {{deficit}} gold.
The chest will answer for {{turnsLeft}}.

variants.headline: Treasury cover: {{turnsLeft}} left
body: In the capital tonight, the treasury holds {{gold}} gold and spends {{deficit}} more than it takes each season. That leaves {{turnsLeft}} of cover. A granary keeper loading the last of the old grain has one question for the {{terms.civic.government}}: who gets paid when the chest is empty?

variants.headline: The old rule was a full store
body: The old rule held that a full store was the best safeguard. Today the store holds {{gold}} gold while {{deficit}} leaves it every season, which is {{turnsLeft}} of cover and no more. Councilors, put the pay and grain bills on the table before you vote another expense, so the trades that fill this city know what work they can take.

variants.headline: The deficit ends
body: The lean run is over. The treasury now keeps {{goldPerTurn}} gold clear of its spending each season. In the barrel yard by the quay, the foreman has taken back a hand he let go in the spring. The board by his door has three names on it again.

variants.headline: The state pays its way
body: The state now clears {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season, after a count that showed it behind. At the customs house, the clerks have stopped holding back the last of each merchant's payment. A wool broker who had priced his fleeces for a lean market raised them by a copper on Thursday and found buyers.

variants.headline: Notice: the accounts no longer run behind
body: Notice is given that the treasury now takes in {{goldPerTurn}} gold more each season than it spends. Traders holding unpaid warrants may present them at the pay office from the opening bell. Bring old warrants before the quarter closes.

variants.headline: The purse that stopped leaking
body: They say a patched purse keeps the coin that a torn one loses. Ours has been patched.

variants.headline: Hear it! The lean stretch is over!
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}, hear it! The chest takes in {{goldPerTurn}} gold more than it spends, and the hard season is done! No more counting coppers by the door, no more holding back the pay! Come and spend what you have earned!
